chunks: What was narrated by Muḥammad ibn Aḥmad ibn Yaḥyā, from Yaʿqūb ibn Yazīd, from ʿAlī ibn al-Nuʿmān, from al-Ḥusayn ibn Abī al-ʿAlāʾ, from Abī ʿAbd Allāh عليه السلام, who said:

I said: I come to the Imam while he had preceded me by one rakʿah in the fajr prayer. Then when he gave salām, it occurred in my heart that I had completed [the prayer], so I continued remembering Allah until the sun rose. Then when it rose, I stood up and remembered that the Imam had preceded me by one rakʿah. He said: If you are still in your place, then complete it with one rakʿah; but if you have already departed, then you must repeat [the prayer].

His statement عليه السلام, 'but if you have already departed, then you must repeat [the prayer],' is to be understood as referring to when he has turned his back to the qiblah. And what is contained in the report of ʿUbayd ibn Zurārah in his statement, 'then he goes and comes,' is to be understood as referring to when he has not turned his back to it. Thus there is no contradiction between them; this detail indicates that.

key_terms.الْإِمَامِ: the prayer leader being followed in congregational salat (prayer)
key_terms.الْقِبْلَةَ: the direction of prayer toward which one must face in salat (prayer)
key_terms.انْصَرَفْتَ: having departed from one’s place after the prayer
key_terms.بِرَكْعَةٍ: one unit of salat (prayer) that remained to be completed

ai.seo_question: What should a person do if he realizes after the Imam’s salām that he missed one rakʿah of fajr prayer?
ai.summary: This hadith addresses a ruling about one who joined the Imam late in the fajr prayer and later realized that one rakʿah remained incomplete. If he is still in his place, he completes the prayer with one rakʿah; if he has departed in a manner implying turning away from the qiblah, he must repeat the prayer. The closing clarification reconciles this report with another narration by distinguishing between departing while still oriented toward the qiblah and fully turning away from it.
